Articles 10/11/13 of China's Teachers Law and Articles 46–48 of the Higher Education Law distinguish qualifications, positions, and appointment. The education requirement for a higher education teaching qualification is graduation from postgraduate study or a university bachelor's program. Those without this level of education have a lawful examination and recognition route; a bachelor's degree alone does not establish eligibility for a job. Articles 2/13 of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications require people specifically engaged in education and teaching to obtain qualifications in accordance with the law and provide for recognition of current or proposed faculty within the institution's authority. Recruitment, professional titles, and appointment contracts require separate checks. Mandarin conditions come from Article 8 of the Implementing Measures for the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications: generally Level Two Grade B or above, Level Three Grade A or above in a few areas with complex dialects, and provincial rules for bilingual teaching in ethnic autonomous areas. Article 9 provides that applicants for recognition who are proposed for associate professor or higher positions at higher education institutions or hold a doctorate need only meet the conditions in 6/7/8(III). They still require recognition and must meet moral conduct, education, and medical examination conditions; this is not an exemption from teaching qualifications.
